steps.question: For each of the mMCP-counter-derived immune and stromal cell populations, does the per-sample abundance score differ significantly between the 6 anti-PD-1-treated and 6 isotype-control tumors, and is this result robust to excluding the low-library sample_01?
acceptance_criteria: Performs an unpaired two-group comparison (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, appropriate given n=6/6 and non-normality risk; report exact p-values) per cell type between anti-PD-1 and control groups, using condition labels from metadata.csv

Applies multiple-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) across all cell types tested and reports both raw and adjusted p-values plus effect size (e.g., rank-biserial correlation or Hodges-Lehmann estimate)

Re-runs the same comparison excluding sample_01 and reports whether any significant or borderline findings change direction or significance, explicitly flagging results that depend on this single sample
Produces a summary table (cell type, group means/medians, test statistic, raw p, adjusted p, robustness flag) and a heatmap or boxplot visualization of per-sample composition split by treatment group
Explicitly states that with n=6 per group this analysis is underpowered for small-to-moderate effect sizes and that any 'significant' findings should be treated as hypothesis-generating

plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal deconvolution: anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon, gene-level raw counts, 12000 genes x 12 mouse samples, MGI symbols) from subcutaneous mouse tumors, 6 anti-PD-1-treated vs 6 isotype-control mice, unpaired single-batch design. The research question asks for immune/stromal cell composition per sample and whether it differs by treatment. Because this is bulk tissue (not single-cell or spatial), the correct approach is reference-based immune deconvolution rather than clustering. sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which is a genuine QC concern for count-based normalization and downstream deconvolution scores, so it must be flagged and handled (down-weighted / sensitivity-checked) rather than silently included or dropped without justification. The plan: (1) QC and normalize the counts (CPM/TPM-scale, appropriate for mouse gene-symbol input, with explicit treatment of the low-library sample), producing a normalized expression matrix in the units immune deconvolution tools expect; (2) run mouse-specific reference-based deconvolution (mMCP-counter, the only well-validated murine-marker-based method for 16 immune/stromal populations, cross-checked against ConsensusTME mouse-orthology-free ssGSEA/singscore of MSigDB mouse immunologic and hallmark immune-relevant gene sets as an orthogonal, marker-based sanity check) to estimate per-sample immune and stromal cell scores; (3) statistically compare each cell population's score between anti-PD-1 and isotype control groups (unpaired, n=6 vs n=6, non-parametric plus effect size given small n, multiple-testing correction across cell types), explicitly re-running with and without sample_01 to test robustness; (4) produce a summary report (heatmap/table of per-sample composition, group comparison statistics, and a QC-robustness note). No reference is available for CIBERSORT/LM22 (human-only) so composition is estimated with the mouse-native and marker-based methods actually available.
